author: revivalfx
text:
Hi All.

I've been reading through this thread and If's document on post 1. Nice thread.

I keep seeing the acronym CPLQ (Compression followed by liquidity) on charts. Liquidity is all the market is. Liquidity is the reason for the support and resistance lines or supply/demand zones. It is the cause of all retraces and bounces. (I have been heavily influenced by the orderflow camp).

Two things that I have picked up: 1.) Compression in itself eats up bits of liquidity (supply/demand) as it goes along. 2.) Many times it does so into a supply/demand zone (an area of lots of liquidity).

So is CPLQ basically number 2 listed above or is it more than that?

Also, from a noob's perspective, compression looks like it is always moving diagonally (like a finishing triangle) with a slight similarity a very tight ranging price and wicks shooting the opposite direction of the price movement (I'm assuming this is true... can you actually have bullish compression with bullish wicks and or bearish wicks?According to If's document "when price taking out last decision point and the orders that where left there." All the examples lead me to believe price is moving away from these decision points. ), all with a slight bullish or bearish direction. Sometimes compression doesn't look like a finishing triangle at all. It looks as though price has sort of lost it's structure somewhat. It looks indecisive, but is making decisions at the same time. Is this too vague and simplistic of a description?

If not, this would exclude very tight ranges (areas of indecision). Compression actually tells you the decision that is being made. Am I making sense?

While I'm at it, my perception is that poles are basically price bursts (very long candle bodies in succession and going the same direction) that are typically the origin of a move. Also, flags look like compression between two poles (I'm assuming this is where the term flag comes from). Correct?

Thanks

P.S. I've edited this post about 20 times. Writing it out seems to help me process things more than pictures. My philosophy on learning is if you can't teach it and communicate it, you don't know it.
